events.text: {name} sits against the bulkhead with a grease pencil and a flask, looking at the dark just past your light. The wall beside them is tallied in fives, a great many fives, in three different hands, and the newest set is {name}'s. 'Don't shine that in my eyes,' {name} says, mildly. 'I've got used to the idea of not seeing.' The air in here is stale but it is air, and somebody has been keeping the scrubber alive with a coat hanger.

choices.text: Sit down beside {name} and say nothing.

outcomes.text: You sit. The hull ticks as it cools. After a long while {name} tells you where the last of the good stock is kept: not a secret, just something nobody had asked about. 'Funny,' {name} says. 'You get used to talking to the wall. The wall never wants to know where anything is.'
You sit. {name} is asleep against your shoulder inside a minute, and you stay until your light starts to go. When {name} wakes there is a small hard pouch pressed into your hand and no mention of it.

choices.text: Ask about the sealed door at the end of the deck.

outcomes.text: 'I sealed it myself,' says {name}. 'It was making a noise and I didn't like the noise. Behind it was storage, once. Maybe it still is.' {name} taps the wall twice, the way you would pat a dog you would rather not meet again.
{name} lifts the pencil in a small salute, and adds one more stroke to the wall.

events.text: A figure in a half-sealed suit, one glove off, is waving a torch slowly back and forth across the deck, the way people wave at a ship that left some time ago. {name} sees your light and stops, then waves harder. The suit seam is split down the left thigh and held with a strip of tape that has given up. 'Tell me,' {name} says, in a voice scraped thin, 'that you have a hull that holds air.'

outcomes.text: {name} leans on you the whole way, breathing like a bellows. 'Can't pay,' {name} manages. 'Can point.' And does, with the bare hand, at a locker, all down the length of the corridor.

choices.text: Reseal the suit with polymer film (3 polymer).

outcomes.text: You cut the film to size and iron it down with the heel of your hand. The seam holds. {name} breathes in, all the way, for what looks like the first time in days, and sits down on the deck rather suddenly. 'I've got stuff,' {name} says. 'You've earned a look at it.'

choices.text: Share your air for a minute.

outcomes.text: You cross the hoses and the two of you breathe from the one line, close as dancers, until {name}'s hands stop shaking. 'I'll remember this,' {name} says, and draws a small map on your glove with a fingertip, in what is left of the condensation.

choices.text: Say the airlock is that way, and go.

outcomes.text: 'Right,' says {name}. 'Right. That way.' The torch starts to wave again behind you.

events.text: {name} is behind a barricade of lockers with a length of pipe and a very clear idea of what you might be. You hold your torch low and still. It takes {name} a long time. 'You're not them,' {name} says at last. 'They don't use torches.' The pipe does not lower. In the dark behind {name} there is a camp bed made up with hospital corners, and a second cup set out, just in case.

outcomes.text: {name} puts the pipe down on a locker, carefully, as if it might wake something. It takes most of an hour. By the end you know the names of nine people who are not here any more, and {name} has made up a mind. 'I can pull a trigger and I can pull a cable,' {name} says. 'Is there room?'
{name} will not be talked down. 'Go on,' {name} says, and keeps saying it, quietly, 'go on, go on,' until it is the only sound on the deck. You go. It was the right thing to have asked.

choices.text: Say you are only here for the cargo.

outcomes.text: {name} lets you pass, with a jerk of the pipe toward the one locker worth having. 'Nobody's touched that,' {name} says. 'Didn't feel right.'
The pipe follows you to the end of the corridor, and then, finally, lets you go.

events.text: {name} has covered a whole bulkhead in chalk: bearings, dates, fuel tallies, columns of numbers in four different hands. 'Don't touch the wall,' {name} says, without turning round. 'It's the only thing in here that's right.' In the corner of the lowest column someone has written LANTERN, crossed it out, and written it again. {name} has a head cold and a chalk-white thumb, and the look of a person who has come back from somewhere.

outcomes.text: 'I went,' {name} says. 'Twice. Copied this off a wall on a ship called Long Odds, and then I went, and then I went again.' The chalk thumb moves down the column. 'Real ones are late. They start late every time, somebody's thumb is on the button. The clean ones are on time.' {name} says the last line to the wall, not to you. 'Don't go to the on-time ones.'
{name} copies one more line onto the sleeve of the suit, to be safe, and comes without a word. The chalk comes too, in a fine white drift, all the way down the corridor.

events.text: {name} is eating cold beans out of a tin with a pocket knife. They see you, and the light, and the dark behind it, and after a pause that seems to cost something they hold out the tin. 'There's more,' {name} says. 'There isn't.' It is the kindest thing anyone has said to you in a corridor this month.

outcomes.text: They are cold, and they are the best thing you have eaten in a week. {name} watches you do it with the shy pleasure of a person who has been allowed to be generous.

choices.text: Ask what is still worth taking aboard.

outcomes.text: 'Cabinets in the next room,' says {name}. 'Hands too cold to try the third drawer. Maybe you'll do better.' A pencilled sheet slides out of a pocket, an air budget, nine names and a long column of sums. {name} lets you copy it.
'Any time,' says {name}, and means every word of it.
